findings.title: Removal of findMany breaks existing callers
findings.body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts the public method findMany(findManyArgs) that performed prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany with authorization plus filter conditions was deleted and replaced by getBaseConditions() returning Prisma.Sql. Any existing caller that imports InsightsBookingService and calls findMany will now fail at compile/runtime with TypeError. More seriously, callers must now manually do prisma.$queryRaw with WHERE ${baseConditions}; if any caller is not migrated or forgets to include the fragment, authorization is silently bypassed. This PR updates no callers.

findings.title: ANY(array) binding without cast can fail in Postgres
findings.body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition build fragments like ("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})) and ("userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds})). A JS number[] is passed as a single bound parameter with no ::int[] cast and without Prisma.join. Postgres cannot always infer the element type of ANY($1), resulting in errors like could not determine data type or operator integer = unknown[]. The PR description states tests were never successfully run, so this is unverified. Consequence is runtime query failure for org/team scoped insights.

findings.title: Org scope test assumes deterministic DB ordering
findings.body: In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts the org-scope expectation compares Prisma.Sql with toEqual, which compares the bound values arrays order-sensitively. The expected teamIds [org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and userIds [user.id, user2.id, user3.id] come from TeamRepository.findAllByParentId and MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds which have no ORDER BY. Database return order is undefined, but ANY() semantics are order-insensitive. Consequence is a flaky test that fails despite correct authorization logic.

findings.title: Event-type filter OR lacks outer parentheses
findings.body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts buildFilterConditions returns Prisma.sql`("eventTypeId" = $) OR ("eventParentId" = $)` with no outer parentheses. getFilterConditions is public. Any direct composition like WHERE ${filter} AND <other> will evaluate AND before OR in SQL, so rows matching eventParentId bypass the other predicate and leak unauthorized/incorrect rows. Current getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but the fragment itself is unsafe to reuse. Fix is to return Prisma.sql`(("eventTypeId" = $) OR ("eventParentId" = $))`.

findings.title: Public options type loses required teamId for team scope
findings.body: In packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts the constructor changed from the discriminated union InsightsBookingServiceOptions (which requires teamId when scope is team) to InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions with optional teamId for all scopes. A call with scope team and missing teamId now compiles and only fails safeParse at runtime to null, which later yields 1=0 and an empty result. Consequence is silent empty insights instead of a compile-time error, hiding caller bugs.
